A.11 Proof of Proposition 3 (LASSO utility)

As in the proof of Proposition 2, we denote the rescaled squared loss by $L(\theta;X,y) := \frac{1}{n\bar{\sigma}}\|y - X\theta\|_2^2$, and by $S_{C_1} := C_1 \cdot \{\pm e_i\}_{i=1}^d$ we denote the set of $2d$ extreme points of the $\ell_1$-ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$, scaled by the constraint $C_1$.

We begin by stating a convergence result for the Frank-Wolfe algorithm due to Jaggi [27], which forms the core of our analysis.

**Lemma 5 ([27]).** Fix $s > 0$ and $\theta_1 \in \mathcal{D} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$. Let $(\phi_1, \ldots, \phi_k)$ be a sequence of vectors from $\mathcal{D}$ and let $\theta_{t+1} = (1 - \Delta_t)\theta_t + \Delta_t\phi_t$, for arbitrary $\Delta_t \in [0,1]$. Define the curvature constant of $L$ as

$$
C _ {L} := \sup  _ {\theta_ {1}, \theta_ {2} \in \mathcal {D}, \gamma \in [ 0, 1 ], \theta_ {3} = (1 - \gamma) \theta_ {1} + \gamma \theta_ {2}} \frac {2}{\gamma^ {2}} \left(L \left(\theta_ {3}\right) - L \left(\theta_ {1}\right) - \left(\theta_ {3} - \theta_ {1}\right) ^ {\top} \nabla L \left(\theta_ {1}\right)\right).
$$

Suppose that for all $t \in [k]$, it holds that: $\phi_t^\top \nabla L(\theta_t) \leq \min_{\phi \in C_1 \cdot \{\pm e_i\}_{i=1}^d} \phi^\top \nabla L(\theta_t) + \frac{s\Delta_tC_L}{2}$. Then,

$$
L \left(\theta_ {k + 1}\right) - \min  _ {\theta : \| \theta \| _ {1} \leq C _ {1}} L (\theta) \leq \frac {2 C _ {L}}{k + 2} (1 + s).
$$

Denote by $b := \frac{4t_{r,1 - \delta / (2d)}C_1\|X\|_{2,\infty}}{n\eta}$ the parameter of the Laplace noise in Algorithm 2. Fix $s > 0$. Denoting by $C_L$ the curvature constant of $L$, as defined in Lemma 5, and by applying subexponential concentration of the Laplace distribution, we know:

$$
\begin{array}{l}
\mathbb {P} \left\{\exists t \in [ k ]: \phi_ {t} ^ {\top} \nabla L \left(\theta_ {t}; X, y\right) > \min  _ {\phi \in S _ {C _ {1}}} \phi^ {\top} \nabla L \left(\theta_ {t}; X, y\right) + \frac {s \Delta_ {t} C _ {L}}{2} \right\} \\
\leq \mathbb {P} \left\{\exists t \in [ k ]: \max  _ {\phi \in S _ {C _ {1}}} | \xi_ {t, \phi} | > \frac {s \Delta_ {t} C _ {L}}{4} \right\} \\
\leq \mathbb {P} \left\{\max  _ {t \in [ k ], \phi \in S _ {C _ {1}}} | \xi_ {t, \phi} | > \frac {s \Delta_ {k} C _ {L}}{4} \right\} \\
\leq k \left| S _ {C _ {1}} \right| \exp \left(- \frac {s \Delta_ {k} C _ {L}}{4 b}\right),
\end{array}
$$

where the last step follows by a union bound. Setting $s = \frac{4b}{\Delta_k C_L} \log (k |S_{C_1}| / \zeta)$ controls this probability to be at most $\zeta$.

We use a standard fact from convex geometry: for any set $S_{\mathcal{D}}$ such that its convex hull is equal to $\mathcal{D}$, it holds that $\min_{\phi \in \mathcal{D}} \phi^{\top} \nabla L(\theta_t; X, y) = \min_{\phi \in S_{\mathcal{D}}} \phi^{\top} \nabla L(\theta_t; X, y)$. In our setting, $\mathcal{D} = \{\theta : \| \theta \|_1 \leq C_1\}$, and it can be obtained as the convex hull of $S_{C_1}$.

With this, we can apply Lemma 5, as well as the fact that $|S_{C_1}| = 2d$, to get that with probability $1 - \zeta$ over the Laplace noise variables:

$$
L \left(\theta_ {k + 1}; X, y\right) - \min  _ {\theta : \| \theta \| _ {1} \leq C _ {1}} L (\theta ; X, y) \leq \frac {2 C _ {L}}{k + 2} + \frac {8 C _ {L} b \log (2 k d / \zeta)}{(k + 2) \Delta_ {k} C _ {L}}.
$$

By the curvature characterization for quadratics due to Clarkson [14], we can bound the curvature constant as

$$

sections.title: A.12 Proof of Proposition 4 (marginal screening stability)
sections.text:
Let $y \sim \mathcal{N}(\mu, \sigma^2 I)$ and define $c_i^\omega \coloneqq \frac{1}{n\hat{\sigma}} X_i^\top \omega$ for all $\omega \in \mathbb{R}^n$. Let $Y_\delta = \{\omega : \| c^\omega - c^\mu \|_\infty \leq \frac{t_{r,1 - \delta/(2d)} \|X\|_{2,\infty}}{n}\}$. First we prove that $\mathbb{P}\{y \in Y_\delta\} \geq 1 - \delta$:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb {P} \left\{\| c ^ {y} - c ^ {\mu} \| _ {\infty} \geq \frac {t _ {r , 1 - \delta / (2 d)} \| X \| _ {2 , \infty}}{n} \right\} &= \mathbb {P} \left\{\exists i: \frac {1}{n \hat {\sigma}} | X _ {i} ^ {\top} y - X _ {i} ^ {\top} \mu | \geq \frac {t _ {r , 1 - \delta / (2 d)} \| X \| _ {2 , \infty}}{n} \right\} \\
&= \mathbb {P} \left\{\exists i: \left| \frac {X _ {i} ^ {\top} (y - \mu)}{\hat {\sigma}} \right| \geq t _ {r, 1 - \delta / (2 d)} \| X \| _ {2, \infty} \right\} \\
&\leq d \cdot \frac {\delta}{d} = \delta .
\end{aligned}
$$

<!-- PAGE BREAK -->

Now we appeal to a similar composition argument as in Proposition 2. From here on, fix $y \in Y_{\delta}$. We will show that the output of stable marginal screening, when applied to $y$, is indistinguishable from the output of stable marginal screening given the oracle input $\mu$.

The selected model $\tilde{M}$ can be written as the output of a composition of $k$ functions $g_{t}(i_{1},\ldots ,i_{t - 1},y)$, $t\in [k]$. In particular, the feature "peeled off" at time $t$, $i_{t}$, is equal to $g_{t}(i_{1},\dots ,i_{t - 1},y)$. We show that $g_{t}(i_{1},\dots ,i_{t - 1},y)\approx_{\eta ,0}g_{t}(i_{1},\dots ,i_{t - 1},\mu)$ holds true for all fixed $i_1,\ldots ,i_{t - 1}$. By Lemma 3, that will imply that the overall selected model under input $y$ and under input $\mu$ is indistinguishable as well.

Fix a round $t \in [k]$, as well as an index $i \in \mathrm{res}_t$. Suppose that we add independent draws $\xi_{t,j} \sim \operatorname{Lap}\left(\frac{2t_{r,1 - \delta/(2d)}\|X\|_{2,\infty}}{n\eta}\right)$ to each value $c_j$, where $j \in \mathrm{res}_t$. Define

$$
\xi_ {+} ^ {*} = \underset {\xi \geq - c _ {i} ^ {y}} {\arg \min } c _ {i} ^ {y} + \xi > | c _ {j} ^ {y} + \xi_ {t, j} |, \quad \xi_ {-} ^ {*} = \underset {\xi < - c _ {i} ^ {y}} {\arg \max } - c _ {i} ^ {y} - \xi > | c _ {j} ^ {y} + \xi_ {t, j} |, \forall j \neq i.
$$

Then, $g_{t}(i_{1},\ldots ,i_{t - 1},y) = i$ if and only if $\xi_{t,i}\geq \xi_{+}^{*}$ or $\xi_{t,i}\leq \xi_{-}^{*}$. Moreover, since $y\in Y_{\delta}$, we have

$$
\frac {t _ {r , 1 - \delta / (2 d)} \| X \| _ {2 , \infty}}{n} + c _ {i} ^ {\mu} + \xi_ {+} ^ {*} \geq c _ {i} ^ {y} + \xi_ {+} ^ {*} > | c _ {j} ^ {y} + \xi_ {t, j} | \geq | c _ {j} ^ {\mu} + \xi_ {t, j} | - \frac {t _ {r , 1 - \delta / (2 d)} \| X \| _ {2 , \infty}}{n},
$$

$$
\frac {t _ {r , 1 - \delta / (2 d)} \| X \| _ {2 , \infty}}{n} - c _ {i} ^ {\mu} - \xi_ {-} ^ {*} \geq - c _ {i} ^ {y} - \xi_ {-} ^ {*} > | c _ {j} ^ {y} + \xi_ {t, j} | \geq | c _ {j} ^ {\mu} + \xi_ {t, j} | - \frac {t _ {r , 1 - \delta / (2 d)} \| X \| _ {2 , \infty}}{n}.
$$

Rearranging the terms, we get

$$
\frac {2 t _ {r , 1 - \delta / (2 d)} \| X \| _ {2 , \infty}}{n} + c _ {i} ^ {\mu} + \xi_ {+} ^ {*} \geq | c _ {j} ^ {\mu} + \xi_ {t, j} |, \frac {2 t _ {r , 1 - \delta / (2 d)} \| X \| _ {2 , \infty}}{n} - c _ {i} ^ {\mu} - \xi_ {-} ^ {*} \geq | c _ {j} ^ {\mu} + \xi_ {t, j} |.
$$

Thus, if $\xi_{t,i} \geq \xi_{+}^{*} + \frac{2t_{r,1 - \delta/(2d)}\|X\|_{2,\infty}}{n}$ or $\xi_{t,i} \leq \xi_{-}^{*} - \frac{2t_{r,1 - \delta/(2d)}\|X\|_{2,\infty}}{n}$, then $i = g_t(i_1,\ldots,i_{t-1},\mu)$ if the noise levels are $(\xi_{t,1},\ldots,\xi_{t,i},\ldots,\xi_{t,d})$. Finally, for fixed $y \in Y_\delta$, we have

$$
\begin{array}{l}
\mathbb {P} \left\{g _ {t} \left(i _ {1}, \dots , i _ {t - 1}, \mu\right) = i \mid \left\{\xi_ {t, j} \right\} _ {j \neq i} \right\} \\
\geq \mathbb {P} \left\{\xi_ {t, i} \geq \xi_ {+} ^ {*} + \frac {2 t _ {r , 1 - \delta / (2 d)} \| X \| _ {2 , \infty}}{n} \mid \{\xi_ {t, j} \} _ {j \neq i} \right\} \\
+ \mathbb {P} \left\{\xi_ {t, i} \leq \xi_ {-} ^ {*} - \frac {2 t _ {r , 1 - \delta / (2 d)} \| X \| _ {2 , \infty}}{n} \mid \{\xi_ {t, j} \} _ {j \neq i} \right\} \\
\geq e ^ {- \eta} \mathbb {P} \left\{\xi_ {t, i} \geq \xi_ {+} ^ {*} \mid \left\{\xi_ {t, j} \right\} _ {j \neq i} \right\} + e ^ {- \eta} \mathbb {P} \left\{\xi_ {t, i} \leq \xi_ {-} ^ {*} \mid \left\{\xi_ {t, j} \right\} _ {j \neq i} \right\} \\
= e ^ {- \eta} \mathbb {P} \left\{g _ {t} \left(i _ {1}, \dots , i _ {t - 1}, y\right) = i \mid \left\{\xi_ {t, j} \right\} _ {j \neq i} \right\}.
\end{array}
$$

Multiplying by $e^{\eta}$ and applying the law of iterated expectations completes the proof that $g_{t}(i_{1},\ldots ,i_{t - 1},y)\approx_{\eta ,0}g_{t}(i_{1},\ldots ,i_{t - 1},\mu)$ for all $y\in Y_{\delta}$.

Finally, by Lemma 3 we conclude that for all fixed $y \in Y_{\delta}$, the output of stable marginal screening under input $y$ and under the oracle input $\mu$ is $\left(\frac{1}{2} k\eta^2 + \sqrt{2k\log(1 / \delta)}\eta, \delta\right)$-indistinguishable for all $\delta \in (0,1)$, or alternatively $(k\eta, 0)$-indistinguishable. Since this holds with $1 - \delta$ probability over the choice of $y$, we see that stable marginal screening satisfies stability with the desired parameters.

sections.title: C Generalizations of stable algorithms
sections.text:
We show how our stable algorithms can be generalized beyond the setting of Gaussianity. Our proofs exploited Gaussianity of the outcome vector only in terms of the decay of its tails. In general we only need

<!-- PAGE BREAK -->

to know how tightly $y$ concentrates around $\mu$ in order to reproduce the stable versions of the LASSO and marginal screening. To show this, we generalize our approach to all outcome vectors with bounded Orlicz norm. This includes other important cases such as general subgaussian and subexponential vectors $y$.

###### Definition 3 (Orlicz norm).

A function $\psi:\mathbb{R}_{\geq}0\to\mathbb{R}_{\geq}0$ is an Orlicz function if $\psi$ is convex, non-decreasing, and satisfies $\psi(0)=0$, $\psi(x)\to\infty$ as $x\to\infty$. For an Orlicz function $\psi$, the Orlicz norm or $\psi$-norm of a random variable $W$ is defined as

$\|W\|_{\psi}=\inf\left\{s>0:\mathbb{E}\left[\psi\left(\frac{|W|}{s}\right)\right]\leq 1\right\}.$

This definition immediately implies a tail bound by Markov’s inequality:

$\mathbb{P}\{|W|\geq s\|W\|_{\psi}\}\leq\mathbb{P}\bigg{\{}\psi\left(\frac{|W|}{\|W\|_{\psi}}\right)\geq\psi(s)\bigg{\}}\leq\frac{\mathbb{E}\left[\psi\left(\frac{|W|}{\|W\|_{\psi}}\right)\right]}{\psi(s)}\leq\frac{1}{\psi(s)}.$ (8)

A natural extension of Definition 3 to random vectors is to consider all one-dimensional projections.

###### Definition 4 (Orlicz norm in $\mathbb{R}^{n}$).

For a random vector $W\in\mathbb{R}^{n}$ and Orlicz function $\psi$, we define the Orlicz norm of $W$ as

$\|W\|_{\psi}=\inf\left\{s>0:\sup_{v\in\mathbb{R}^{n}:\|v\|_{2}\leq 1}\|W^{\top}v\|_{\psi}\leq s\right\}.$

We state a corollary of Theorem 2, where we construct confidence intervals for stable selection methods as long as the outcomes have bounded $\psi$-norm, for some Orlicz function $\psi$.

###### Corollary 3.

Suppose $\|y-\mu\|_{\psi}\leq G$, for some known $G>0$, and fix $\delta\in(0,1)$. Let $\hat{M}$ be an $(\eta,\tau,\nu)$-stable model selection algorithm. For all $j\in\hat{M}$, let

$\mathrm{CI}_{j\cdot\hat{M}}=\left(\hat{\beta}_{j\cdot\hat{M}}\pm\psi^{-1}\left(|\hat{M}|e^{\eta}/\delta\right)G\sqrt{((X_{\hat{M}}^{\top}X_{\hat{M}})^{-1})_{jj}}\right).$

Then

$\mathbb{P}\Big{\{}\exists j\in\hat{M}\ :\ \beta_{j\cdot M}\not\in\mathrm{CI}_{j\cdot\hat{M}}\Big{\}}\leq\delta+\tau+\nu.$

###### Proof.

Fix a model $M$. We only need to argue that

$\mathbb{P}\Bigg{\{}\max_{j\in M}\left|\frac{\hat{\beta}_{j\cdot M}-\beta_{j\cdot M}}{G\sqrt{((X_{\hat{M}}^{\top}X_{\hat{M}})^{-1})_{jj}}\right|\geq\psi^{-1}\left(|M|e^{\eta}/\delta\right)\Bigg{\}}\leq\delta e^{-\eta}.$

Invoking Theorem 2 then completes the proof.

Denote by $X_{j\cdot M}$ the residual vector when $X_{j}$ is regressed onto all other variables in $M$; that is, $X_{j\cdot M}=P_{X_{M\setminus j}}^{\perp}X_{j}$, where $P_{X_{M\setminus j}}^{\perp}$ denotes the projection matrix onto the orthocomplement of $X_{M\setminus j}$. With this notation, we can express the least-squares solution as

$\hat{\beta}_{j\cdot M}=\frac{X_{j\cdot M}^{\top}y}{\|X_{j\cdot M}\|_{2}^{2}},\ \ \beta_{j\cdot M}=\frac{X_{j\cdot M}^{\top}\mu}{\|X_{j\cdot M}\|_{2}^{2}}.$

Moreover, $\left(X_{M}^{\top}X_{M}\right)_{jj}^{-1}=\frac{1}{\|X_{j\cdot M}\|_{2}^{2}}$. Using this fact, we have

$\mathbb{P}\Bigg{\{}\max_{j\in M}\left|\frac{\hat{\beta}_{j\cdot M}-\beta_{j\cdot M}}{G\sqrt{((X_{\hat{M}}^{\top}X_{\hat{M}})^{-1})_{jj}}\right|\geq\psi^{-1}\left(|M|e^{\eta}/\delta\right)\Bigg{\}}$
$=\mathbb{P}\left\{\max_{j\in M}|v_{j\cdot M}^{\top}(y-\mu)|\geq G\psi^{-1}\left(|M|e^{\eta}/\delta\right)\right\},$

<!-- PAGE BREAK -->

where we define  $v_{j\cdot M}$  to be the random unit vector  $\frac{X_{j\cdot M}}{\|X_{j\cdot M}\|_2}$ . By applying the tail bound given by Eq. (8) together with a union bound, we get

$$
\begin{array}{l} \mathbb {P} \left\{\max  _ {j \in M} | v _ {j \cdot M} ^ {\top} (y - \mu) | \geq G \psi^ {- 1} \left(| M | e ^ {\eta} / \delta\right) \right\} \leq \sum_ {j \in M} \mathbb {P} \left\{| v _ {j \cdot M} ^ {\top} (y - \mu) | \geq \psi^ {- 1} \left(| M | e ^ {\eta} / \delta\right) \right\} \\ \leq | M | \left(\psi \left(\psi^ {- 1} \left(| M | e ^ {\eta} / \delta\right)\right)\right) ^ {- 1} \\ = \delta e ^ {- \eta}. \\ \end{array}
$$

Now we can generalize the stable versions of the LASSO and marginal screening. We state counterparts of Algorithm 2 and Algorithm 3 which ensure stability as long as we know a bound  $G$  on  $\| y - \mu \|_{\psi}$ .

Algorithm 6 Stable LASSO algorithm under general Orlicz norm  $\psi$
input: design matrix  $X\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$  , outcome vector  $y\in \mathbb{R}^n$ $\ell_1$  -constraint  $C_1$  , number of optimization steps  $k$  , typical stability parameters  $\delta \in (0,1),\eta >0$
output: LASSO solution  $\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{LASSO}}\in \mathbb{R}^d$
Initialize  $\theta_{1} = 0$
for  $t = 1,2,\ldots ,k$  do
$\forall \phi \in C_1\cdot \{\pm e_i\}_{i = 1}^d$  sample  $\xi_{t,\phi}\stackrel {\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mathrm{Lap}\left(\frac{4\psi^{-1}(1 / \delta)C_1\|X\|_{2,\infty G}}{n\eta}\right)$ $\forall \phi \in C_1\cdot \{\pm e_i\}_{i = 1}^d$  , let  $\alpha_{\phi} = \frac{2}{n}\phi^{\top}X^{\top}(y - X\theta_{t}) + \xi_{t,\phi}$  Set  $\phi_t = \arg \min_{\phi \in C_1\cdot \{\pm e_i\}_{i = 1}^d}\alpha_\phi$  Set  $\theta_{t + 1} = (1 - \Delta_t)\theta_t + \Delta_t\phi_t$  , where  $\Delta_t = \frac{2}{t + 2}$
end
Return  $\hat{\theta}_{\mathrm{LASSO}} = \theta_{k + 1}$

Algorithm 7 Stable marginal screening algorithm under general Orlicz norm  $\psi$
input: design matrix  $X\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times d}$  , outcome vector  $y\in \mathbb{R}^n$  , model size  $k$
output:  $\hat{M} = \{i_1,\dots ,i_k\}$
Compute  $(c_{1},\ldots ,c_{d}) = \frac{1}{n} X^{\top}y\in \mathbb{R}^{d}$
$\mathrm{res}_1 = [d]$
for  $t = 1,2,\ldots ,k$  do
$\forall i\in \mathrm{res}_i$  sample  $\xi_{t,i}\stackrel {\mathrm{i.i.d.}}{\sim}\mathrm{Lap}\left(\frac{2\psi^{-1}(1 / \delta)\|X\|_{2,\infty G}}{n\eta}\right)$ $i_t = \arg \max_{i\in \mathrm{res}_t}|c_i + \xi_{t,i}|$ $\mathrm{res}_{t + 1} = \mathrm{res}_t\setminus i_t$
end
Return  $\hat{M} = \{i_1,\dots ,i_k\}$
